description: Draw a picture in any application that can draw (Paint, AutoCAD, PowerPoint, Word, Excel, SVG/PNG files) from one source: a photo, an SVG, a template or objects.

tools.name: art.draw
tools.description: Draw ANY picture in ANY application that can draw, in ONE call, at maximum detail by default. app: 'paint' (Microsoft Paint, mouse-drawn filled polygons), 'autocad' (line-only: a coloured pencil sketch, every stroke in the colour of what it depicts, hidden lines removed), 'powerpoint' | 'word' | 'excel' (editable freeform shapes in any colour: the most detailed result), 'file' (writes SVG + PNG for any other program: Inkscape, Illustrator, Photoshop, GIMP, Krita, Figma, Canva, a browser). Give exactly ONE picture source: image_path (a photo or picture file: traced to colour regions), svg (a picture YOU write as SVG), svg_path (an .svg file), template ('doraemon' | 'house') or objects (same format as paint.draw). WRITING THE SVG (when there is no source picture): viewBox "0 0 1000 562.5"; first a background <rect>, then shapes from big to small: body, head, then ears, limbs, clothes, then eyes, nose, mouth, details, last highlights and shadows; build figures from overlapping <ellipse>, <circle> and closed <path> curves (C/Q/A commands), not from rectangles; give every part its own shape, a darker outline (stroke-width 2-4) and, on big parts, an extra lighter highlight shape and a darker shade shape; parts must touch or overlap their neighbours (ears overlap the head, legs the body: no gaps or floating pieces); mirror symmetric subjects around x=500; the subject fills about 80% of the height; 40-150 shapes for a detailed picture; real colours (fur, skin, sky) not primary colours. Only plain shapes are drawn (no text, filters, masks, images). style 'auto' (default): filled where the application can fill, coloured pencil sketch where it can only draw lines; 'sketch' only when the user asks for a sketch. Never lower detail on your own. The drawing is verified (canvas / slide compared with the picture, shapes read back) and reports the likeness (fidelity.ssim); a mismatch fails with VERIFICATION_FAILED. The result includes a screenshot: LOOK at it; if a part is detached, misplaced, out of proportion or too plain, fix the SVG and call art.draw again (reuse_window true in Paint).

app.description: paint | autocad | powerpoint | word | excel | file (also accepted: mspaint, ppt, dwg, svg, png, inkscape, illustrator, photoshop, gimp, krita, figma).

image_path.description: Absolute path of the picture (png, jpg, webp, bmp, gif).

svg.description: A complete <svg ...>...</svg> document you wrote for this picture.

detail.description: Leave unset: the most detailed level the application can take (ultra for Office/file, max for Paint). Lower ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a quick or rough version.

colors.description: Colours of a traced photo for true-colour applications (default 64).

outline.description: Dark outline around every traced region (default: yes in Paint, no elsewhere).

reuse_window.description: paint: draw on the window opened by the previous call.

new_document.description: autocad: open a new drawing (false: draw into the active one).

paper.description: autocad: white model-space background so every colour shows (restored value is reported).

width.description: autocad: sheet width in drawing units (default 1000).

shading.description: autocad: hatch the coloured regions (default yes).

output_path.description: app 'file' only: base path of the .svg/.png pair (default: the task's artifact folder). Documents in PowerPoint/Word/Excel are left open and unsaved; save them with desktop.save_as only when the user asks.

tools.name: art.brief
tools.description: ALWAYS call this first when the user asks to draw / paint / sketch anything in Paint with an artistic intent (a named painting, a style, a medium). It classifies the request (existing artwork / real subject / invention / school / medium), identifies a named work (title, artist, year, movement, medium, what makes it recognisable, palette), decides the goal (REPRODUCTION | STUDY | INTERPRETATION | ADAPTATION | INSPIRED_BY), the medium and the RENDERING MODE (pencil, ink, oil, watercolour, lacquer, flat colour...), honours explicit wishes ("bút chì", "trắng đen", "không tô màu") over its own choice, and downloads a reference picture of a real work from Wikimedia Commons when one is needed (data.image_path). If data.questions is not empty, ask the user (task.ask_user) before drawing: the title names several works. Pass what you already know (artwork_title, artist, medium, style, intent). Verification states are honest: BUILTIN_KNOWLEDGE and UNVERIFIED are not proof.

image_path.description: A reference picture the user supplied.

fetch.description: Download a reference picture of an identified real work.

tools.name: art.paint
tools.description: Draw a picture in Microsoft Paint in a chosen RENDERING MODE, with Paint's real brushes (Oil brush, Crayon, Marker, Natural pencil, Watercolour brush, Calligraphy...; only those this Paint offers), from a reference picture (image_path, e.g. from art.brief) or an SVG. Modes: PENCIL_SKETCH / CHARCOAL_SKETCH (grey hatching, no colour), INK_LINE_ART (black only), BLACK_WHITE, GRAYSCALE, FLAT_COLOR, PAINTERLY, OIL_PAINT_SIMULATION (directional overlapping strokes), ACRYLIC_SIMULATION, WATERCOLOR_SIMULATION (pale washes, paper left white), LACQUER_ART_SIMULATION (black/red/gold with eggshell), TECHNICAL_ILLUSTRATION, PIXEL_ART, HYBRID_RENDERING. Use the mode art.brief chose. The call opens a fresh Paint window, plans, draws in batches, checks the canvas against the plan, recovers from lost focus / open menus / zoom changes, refuses a bucket fill whose region is not closed, and reports what it did. It is a visual simulation: say so in the answer (Paint has no real oil, watercolour or lacquer). Takes several minutes for brush modes. After it succeeds finish with task.complete using the call as evidence.

resume.description: With reuse_window: look at the canvas first and draw only what is not there.

brief.description: The data object returned by art.brief (kept in the specification as the source of identity, intent and verification state).
